Twenty-three year old Peter Willis made his first appearance in a Belgrave team – the ‘C’s – and exactly equalled the time set by Knut Hegvold in the ‘B’s; more young blood for the cross-country season ahead.

The Skipper managed to slot into a position he hadn’t filled before – 13th – to confound the predictions and wily Knut Hegvold paced his race perfectly to get up to 20th, ahead of a disappointed Peter Willis who’d had the better of Knut on the roads of Rushmoor Arena.

Pete Willis ran like a man possessed as he tried to keep the Bs ahead of the As. For almost the whole of the first lap Al Stewart did not get onto terms with him but the inevitable did eventually occur and the remainder of Pete's race was spent trying to recover from that early burst.

The Skipper looked particularly mean as he chased hard for 14th and with Peter Willis up 12 places on his Brockwell Park position we had enough early men to ensure that we maintained our third spot in the league.
